items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to permitting the parents of pupils attending a persistently lowest-achieving school to choose an education intervention model
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5777

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the education law, in relation to permitting the parents of
pupils attending a persistently lowest-achieving school to choose an
education intervention model

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:
Permits the parents of pupils
attending a persistently lowest achieving school in the city of
Buffalo to choose an educational intervention model.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:
The education law is amended by adding a new section 3613. This
section would mandate that "PLA" schools identified by the
commissioner as persistently lowest achieving and that are required
to implement a federal education intervention model in accordance
with eligibility requirements established for federal education
improvement grants shall permit the parents or legal guardians of
pupils attending such PLA school to choose which intervention model
shall be implemented: the turnaround model, restart model or
transformation model. Implementation of the desired model would be
based upon at least fifty-five percent of the parents and legal
guardians voting and signing a petition identifying the supported
model. These provisions apply to cities with a population of more
than two hundred twenty-five thousand and less than three hundred
thousand.

JUSTIFICATION:
The District Parenting Council of Buffalo and educational advocates in
WNY support the expansion of parental ability to collaborate and
implement new strategies aimed at turning around PLA schools and
improving upon the 31% graduation rates of black male students within
the city of Buffalo.

Parental trigger legislation gives parents more authority to make the
best choices possible in implementing structural changes to the PLA
school that their children attend. This gives parents of the city of
Buffalo more direct involvement the course of their children's
education.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
None.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
